commits.message:
Refuse activate-operator before the activation time instead of waiting

An activation attempted before the operator's activation time now fails
at once with a one-line refusal naming the activation time and the chain
time, in the shape the other operator entry verbs use, rather than
sleeping until the time arrives. Registering and activating in one verb
keeps its wait, since a fresh registration can never have reached its
time yet. Emulator tests cover the refusal and the activation once the
chain time is reached.

Bump lucid-evolution to 0.6.5 and test that a registration cannot prove its own duplication

lucid 0.6.5 (provider 0.2.4) makes the emulator apply the ledger's rule
that a transaction's reference inputs are disjoint from its inputs when a
PlutusV3 script runs, so the emulator now refuses a duplicate-operator
slash whose proof is the node being removed, exactly as the ledger does.
The operator-exit emulator suite asserts that refusal.

The workspace patch on lucid moves to the 0.6.5 key; it applies
unchanged. The nine packages that pin lucid move together.

Assemble manifest-bound linear family workflows from one definition table

One assembly module now builds a linear family's manifest-bound workflow
from a frozen family definition: bind the verified manifest, check the
signer, bind every spec step and declared witness reference script (and
the field-preimage certificate mint when declared), start the L1
observation port, build the family's transaction port and adapter, then
apply the declared prerequisites in a fixed order, field carriage before
proof chunks. A generic run-or-resume hands the workflow's replayer,
single-category launch scope, terminal verifier and release-finality
authority to the retained-DA runner.

The definition is separate from the linear family spec and keyed by
category; step contract names come from the spec and are never
re-declared. It carries step datum schemas, witness roles, the
replayer, the adapter arm (linear implemented, cursor typed but not yet
assembled), one or more field-carriage requirement callbacks, an
optional proof-chunk callback and an optional extend hook. Spec steps
are now tuple-typed so a family's step count is visible to the
reference-script types.

Fabricated deposit, fabricated withdrawal and no-reference-input are
reduced to their transaction port plus definition; their constructor and
type names remain as aliases over the generic ones. Two deliberate
surface changes ride along: the fabricated families' configs now accept
the optional replay context the generic config carries, and their
"manifest omitted required contracts" check runs when the transaction
port is built, after reference binding, instead of directly after the
signer check. Neither changes any submitted transaction. The definitions
table carries a satisfies guard against the linear category list behind
an explicit allow-list of the sixteen families still to migrate.

A table-driven test replaces the two-family fabricated reference-binding
test: fake deployment binding, exact reference binding before provider
startup, missing/moved/forged refusals, declared-prerequisite chain
order and the retained-DA runner hand-off, for every migrated family.
Glossary gains "family definition" and "manifest-bound family assembly".

Refs #654

Operator exit, watchdog and status, with in-flight watcher and fault-proof work

Operator lifecycle (node, SDK, docs): voluntary and forced retirement,
duplicate-registration slashing, bond recovery, scheduler rewind onto
the surviving tail, inactivity strikes with the strike-cap refusal, the
operator watchdog fiber (on by default, OPERATOR_WATCHDOG_ENABLED and
OPERATOR_WATCHDOG_PATIENCE_MS, slot-aware deferral, manifest verified
at start), GET /operator/status with nextPatienceTakeoverTime, the
funding preflight, exact-fee construction with the three-coin collateral
cap, and lucid-evolution emulator suites in both polarities.

A lone registration cannot prove its own duplication: the proof is a
reference input and the removed node is an input, and the ledger keeps
the two disjoint. The validator, node and docs now state that rule as
the guarantee. The emulator-side negative test lands with the lucid pin
bump that carries the emulator fix.

Also included: the finalizer Q56/Q58 local readiness gates removed per
the release-plumbing simplicity ruling, and the in-flight watcher,
fault-proof, node-tools, da-committee-node and core changes from the
parallel sessions. All packages typecheck; the seven operator suites
pass; the other packages' suites were not rerun for this commit.
Record the five families with completed live watcher journeys

Requeue a fault-proof job whose run failed before its journal

The supervisor marked every run finished in the queue journal, including
one that threw before writing a single workflow record. The next process
then computed the same job identity, read the durable finish, and never
ran the proof again while the watcher reported ready. Leave a failed
run's registration active so the next process requeues it, and reopen a
finished registration whose workflow directory holds no execution.

Bind the complete-replay historical corpus to the block, not one object

The header classifier admits the historical native-script corpus against
the evidence it routed, but a family workflow that reuses that admitted
context re-fetches the same challenged block from retained DA. The corpus
check compared the two evidence objects by identity and refused the live
mintAuthorization workflow with 'historical corpus was not admitted for
this challenged header'. Compare the header hash and payload digests
instead, as the predecessor authority already does.

Rebuild an elapsed staged fault before its journey commit

A journey resumed from a checkpoint that was staged by an earlier attempt
still carries that attempt's fault block. Its header end time bounds the
commit's validity interval, so once it has elapsed the commit fails local
evaluation instead of expiring unminted. Rebuild the fault when its
interval has passed and nothing was signed or referenced.

Re-onboard the journey operator when a resumed fault finds its active node slashed

A confirmed slashing correction from an earlier journey spends the
publisher's active-operator node. A staging checkpoint whose predecessor is
still the tail resumed without onboarding and then failed to commit its
fault against the missing node. The actor now reports whether the node is
published and the resumed path onboards again when it is not.

Bind the network-id removal action to the slash funding authority by its shared out-ref names

The production funding reservation permit matches a slashing removal
against the action's nextRemovalOutRef and fraudProofOutRef, while the
network-id adapter issued its removal action under its own field names and
without a stage field, so every live network-id removal was refused. The
adapter now emits the shared names, the permit reads the action kind the
same way everywhere else (actionKind or stage) instead of also demanding a
stage field, and a refusal names the checks that differ.

Anchor the local user-event history before its retained closure reaches the publish bound

Every retained entry pins its own durable-store snapshot, so the retained
closure grows with the store as well as with the entry count. The runtime
only rotated at 128 entries, which let the 128 MiB publish bound refuse
first on a long-lived deployment and stall the watcher. The history view
now reports the retained closure and whether an anchor is due (more than
the 64-entry suffix retained and either the active bound reached or any
closure dimension at half its bound); the runtime rotates on that flag and
ends a round early once it becomes due.

Resolve unconfirmed network-id submissions through signed-transaction recovery

The network-id reconcile answered not_found the moment a submitted
transaction was not yet visible on chain, which made the watcher abandon
its funding transition and rebuild an identical handoff that then collided
with the abandoned one. Route the unconfirmed path through the shared
signed-transaction recovery so a pending or unknown submission keeps the
action waiting, expiry alone yields not_found, and conflicts fail the
mutation lease.

Pin the captured signed transaction on the network-id and double-spend preflights

Drive each adapter's real preflight with the submit module stubbed to
hand the pre-submit boundary a reference-script-only signed body, and
assert the returned preflight resolves that body through
workflowPreflightTransaction. Both tests fail without the binding.

Bind the captured signed transaction to the network-id and double-spend preflights

The production funding reservation permit reconciles the reserved inputs
a proof transaction actually spends by reading the signed body back from
the in-memory preflight. Every other adapter binds that body through
bindWorkflowPreflightTransaction; network-id and double-spend returned
bare preflight views, so the live watcher stalled at funding reservation
with "production preflight omitted its captured signed transaction".
Bind the capture in both adapters.

Label network-id workflow actions with the stable actionKind the funding permit reads

The production funding reservation permit derives every reservation's
action label from the action input's actionKind (or stage) and refuses
an action that carries neither. The network-id adapter was the only
family labelling its actions with a private kind field, so the live
watcher stalled at the init preflight with "production workflow action
omitted its stable action kind". Emit actionKind alongside kind and pin
it in the chain-state action selection test.
